people.name: Abriana M. Gresham, Ph.D.
people.bio: Abriana Gresham is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Humanities and Social Sciences at New Jersey Institute of Technology (NJIT). She completed her Ph.D. in Experimental Psychology (Health Specialization) at Ohio University in 2024 and went on to complete postdoctoral training at Virginia Commonwealth University's Injury and Violence Prevention Research and Evaluation Core before joining NJIT in 2025 and establishing the THREAD Lab.

people.name: Mariam Eleish
people.bio: Mariam is a biology major at NJIT and has been a member of the THREAD Lab since Fall 2025. She is interested in interpersonal dynamics and the ways social experiences can influence health and well-being. Outside of the lab, Mariam enjoys volunteering in her community and exploring her interests in dentistry and healthcare.

people.name: Ria Saketh
people.bio: Ria is a computer engineering major at NJIT and has been a member of the THREAD lab since Spring 2026. She is interested in the intersection of technology and psychology, as well as data analytics. Outside of the lab, Ria works as a tutor in the Norma J. Clayton Learning Center.

people.name: Sahana Jayakanthan
people.bio: Sahana is a biology major at NJIT and has been a member of the THREAD lab since Spring 2026. She is interested in relationship psychology and how it affects individual outcomes for both partners. Outside of the lab, Sahana enjoys helping develop leadership skills in young women through the GirlUp NJIT chapter, working on various art projects, and collecting physical music media.

people.name: Manreet Kaur Bindra
people.bio: Manreet Kaur Bindra is a biology major with a minor in psychology at NJIT. As an undergraduate researcher in the THREAD Lab, she is interested in understanding how relationships and lived experiences influence mental and physical health. She is also a member of NJIT's Urban Ecology Lab, where she explores the connections between people and their environments. Manreet plans to pursue a Ph.D. in neuroscience and hopes to build a career at the intersection of biology, psychology, medicine, and research. Her long-term research interests include the neural basis of human behavior and neuropsychological disorders such as Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, and ADHD.

people.name: Aashna Victoria Balachandran
people.bio: Aashna is a biochemistry major at NJIT and has been a member of the THREAD lab since 2026. She is interested in interpersonal relationships. Outside of the lab, she is on the E-board of NJIT's Psyche and Cycle and enjoys photography, hiking, and going to the gym.

people.name: Akanksha Rajagopal
people.bio: Akanksha is a biology major, with a psychology minor, at NJIT and has been a member of the THREAD lab since 2026. She is interested in the intersection of psychology and physiology: particularly how physiological measures can be interpreted to learn about psychological states. She is also an undergraduate researcher in the Barden Lab at NJIT, where she focuses on the relationships between social behavior and morphological variation in shrimp. Apart from research, Akanksha is the External PR Manager for NJIT's Knit 'n Crochet club and Captain of NJIT's First Aid Squad. She is also passionate about fiber arts, scrapbooking, and music

teamIntro: The THREAD Lab is made up of researchers with diverse training backgrounds and perspectives who are dedicated to understanding the intersection of close relationships, stress, and health. Together, we share an interest in understanding how interpersonal and affective experiences shape well-being across the lifespan. We collaborate on study design, data collection, and dissemination of findings.
workIntro: Research in the THREAD Lab focuses on stress-related and health-relevant processes in the context of close relationships. We pay particular attention to how interpersonal experiences and affect regulation together shape physical health and general well-being. We use multi-method, immersive, and longitudinal approaches to understand these dynamics and their impact. Click below to view our ongoing and completed projects as well as publications and presentations from our lab. ​
project: In collaboration with Dr. Ana DiGiovanni at Montclair State University , we collected data from participants three times per week across the 9-weeks surrounding the major US holiday season (November 2025 - January 2026). We are in the process of analyzing these data to examine a number of research questions, such as: how does conflict ebb and flow across the holiday season? are there differences between conflict and tension? are there differences in experienced conflict based on relationship type (i.e., family, friends, romantic partners)? ​ Learn more about the project here .
